themes.consensus_view: Banks across desks flag Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz oil supply disruption as a live macro catalyst, but only ING stakes a directional view that the market is underpricing it.

evidence_quotes: The oil market continues to reprice ongoing supply disruptions

facts_agreed.claim: Banks frame the disruption as a broader energy / supply shock with inflationary and stagflationary implications.

themes.consensus_view: Most banks see the AI hyperscaler spending boom as a real, structural earnings driver, but a minority warn that hedge funds are crowded into the same trade and capex is eating nearly all of big tech's cash flow.

evidence_quotes: AI spending meanwhile still looks extremely strong.
The upward revision to capex expectations has been dramatic.
AI is very real and the revenues are staggering
AI component of S&P 500 earnings is sizable, strong, and generally insulated against Middle East impacts.
AI infrastructure buildout theme is currently superseding traditional cyclical considerations.
AI investment boom continues to drive a powerful capex cycle

facts_agreed.claim: AI-linked spending is structural rather than cyclical and supports US growth.
evidence_quotes: AI-related spending is more structural than cyclical and provides resiliency amid geopolitical uncertainty.
AI capex has exhibited limited cyclicality and has accounted for the bulk of recent growth
The AI capex boom is driving US growth along with wealth-fueled consumption spending.

higher for longer rates is a problem for equities
